relevance_note: Case report of one girl carrying a TNFAIP3 variant: 'The analysis identified a likely pathogenic variant in TNFAIP3'.
method_note: Read the whole paper (single-patient case report, no supplementary section); rows were written by hand into a short Python builder script, Table 1 values were checked against the table by eye. Label 'patient' per label rule 5. Only Table 1 (laboratory parameters, two parameter/result column pairs) holds patient data; spans quote 'parameter | result' segments. Variants in PIK3R1, HBB, SERPINA1 and VPS37A are attributed to the patient without any variant description, so each has one row with variant_original_string 'not reported' (the paper does not say how many variants per gene). variant_type_as_stated, zygosity and inheritance left 'not reported': the authors do not classify or state zygosity for this variant (only generic statements that HA20 is caused by heterozygous variants), and parental Sanger testing was planned but not done. age_at_last_evaluation is the age at presentation/report ('5-year-old'); treatment then continued for several months of colchicine and an eight-month infliximab follow-up, so the true age at last evaluation is later and not stated. Checklist judgements: 'central nervous system involvement' = observed from the infantile febrile convulsive seizure, which the authors say may be comorbid or coincidental; 'elevated inflammatory markers' = observed from 'CRP | Weakly Positive' (ESR 14 mm/hr not interpreted by the authors); 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' left not reported because ANA negative and celiac serology negative are narrower than the composite item; 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' = excluded from the negative GI investigation and no IBD findings, although abdominal pain, diarrhea and perianal swelling 'resembling hemorrhoidal inflammation' were observed (authors speculate perianal involvement may be an extension of GI mucosal inflammation); 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' left not reported because eye redness/pain and eyelid swelling during episodes sit alongside a negative ophthalmologic investigation. Unlabelled numeric labs (Hb 10.6 g/dL, ALP 408 U/L, IgG, etc.) were not turned into features because the paper does not call them abnormal. Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: (1) onset given as 'from age 2' (Abstract, Introduction) but 'from the age of second year' (Case Presentation), and the title says 'Infantile Onset'; (2) TNFAIP3 variant called 'likely pathogenic' (Abstract, Case Presentation), 'a pathogenic variant' (Introduction) and 'probable pathogenic variants' (Discussion); (3) PIK3R1/HBB/SERPINA1 variants 'considered to play a potential modifier role' (Case Presentation) and 'possibly modifying the phenotype' (Abstract) versus 'They do not modify or explain the core HA20 phenotype' (Discussion). cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = false based on the authors' statement that this is the first report from northeast of Iran.

treatment_summary.value: Phenobarbital for four months in early infancy for a febrile convulsive seizure; colchicine and intermittent courses of prednisolone without meaningful improvement; after genetic diagnosis, infliximab 5 mg/kg at weeks 0, 2 and 6 then maintenance infusions every eight weeks, colchicine discontinued and corticosteroids tapered, with significant clinical improvement (only one self-limited febrile episode over an eight-month follow-up).
